headline: Scandium demand driven by solid oxide fuel cells for AI data centres, aluminium alloys for aerospace and defence, and 5G/6G telecoms infrastructure
reasoning: Scandium is described as a rare earth metal with primary demand coming from solid oxide fuel cells which are increasingly important for AI data centres being built globally. It also alloys with aluminium to produce lighter and stronger materials, with critical applications in aeronautical, defence and automotive industries. Additionally, scandium is used in 5G and 6G telecommunications networks, underpinning a broad and growing demand profile across multiple strategic sectors.
quote: Scandium's a rare earth metal. It's used primarily for solid oxide fuel cells, which are very important for the AI data centres coming being built around the world at the moment. It also alloys with aluminium to make aluminium lighter and stronger. So has critical applications in aeronautical industry, defence, auto industry and it's also used in 5G and 6G, new new wave, 5G and 6G networks for telecommunications.
episode_title: Why Hawk Resources is betting on scandium supply

headline: Exercised 80% option on Olympus Scandium project in WA; exploration starting imminently with soil sampling followed by drilling if results positive
reasoning: Hawk Resources has secured all necessary approvals including native title and cultural heritage surveys for the Olympus Scandium project near the Great Central Highway in WA. The company exercised its option on the project after completing the approval process and plans to begin exploration within weeks. First-stage work involves resampling historical soil sample lines where previous explorers found highly anomalous scandium results, with second-stage drilling to follow if results are positive. Historical reconnaissance drilling and XRF assays show scandium grades similar in tenor to Sunrise Energy Metals' more advanced NSW project. The company notes there are currently no primary scandium mines in the world, with all scandium produced as a byproduct, making the asset strategically significant.
quote: There are actually currently no primary scandium mines in the world, so it's all produced as byproduct. Probably the company that will develop the first scandium deposit in the world is Sunrise Energy Metals, which has a project in New South Wales. And obviously with that, that's the benchmark in terms of what we're trying to achieve with our projects. So we're not comparing apples with apples in terms of they're far more advanced than what we are in terms of the work that's been done. We're much earlier stage, but we're in the right, we believe that we're in the right ballpark. The geological setting is simpler. The grades of the mineralisation that we're getting out of the historical PXRF results and they are only handheld XRF, they're not lab results, are similar sort of tenor to what they've got in terms of their much more advanced project.
